newsitem.title: USA: Campbell Soup more willing to leave NJ.
newsitem.headline: Campbell Soup more willing to leave NJ.

text.p: Campbell Soup Co may move its headquarters out of Camden, New Jersey, where it was founded 128 years ago, spokesman Kevin Lowery said.

Former Chief Executive Officer John Dorrance, grandson of the company's founder, had promised to build new headquarters in Camden. He made the commitment after a land swap with General Electric Co gave him control of the riverfront site once occupied by an RCA factory across the Delaware River from Phildelphia.
The state of New Jersey has been seeking to buy that site and the site of Campbell's former Camden factory, also on the river, for about $5 million.
Continuing leaks about the negotiations from state officals have raised Campbell's willingness to to consider other states, Lowery said.
"They have forced us to listen to overtures we're constantly getting from other states.
"In the past we have not given them as much attention as we are now."
